To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Tekirdag segment of the NAF has a recurrence interval of about three hundred years and the Central Basin of the Marmara sea has been affected by a number of earthquakes in the past.

we obtained a record of turbidity flows that were triggered by the seismicity of the NAF in the Marmarasea and that we dated the turbidites to the 1912 M = 7,4 earthquake and to an earlier earthquake that occurred around 1400 yr ago.
the sedimentary record in five cores from the Marmara sea shows a recurrence interval of 300 years for the Tekirdag and Central segments of the North Anatolia Fault.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and dating of seismo-turidites, which are triggered by the seismic slip along the NAF, and with the implications of the obtained results for seismic hazard assessment.
the identification, characterization and correlation of seismo-turbidites in the western part (Tekirdag Basin and the Central Basin) of the Sea of Marma.
the seismic hazard in Istanbul, and the obtained data can be integrated with other paleoseismological studies and seismic data to provide a more accurate seismic hazard assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Tekirdag segment ruptured at 1912, 1943, 1766, 1688, and 1458 AD, and probably at 1224 AD.
the 1912 M = 7 4 earthquake ruptured the Tekirdag and the adjacent Central segments of the NAF, but the recurrence interval of the Tekirda segment is not known.

the M = 8.3 earthquake of 1766, which was a rupture of the entire North Anatolian Fault System, was the last earthquake along the Tekirdagh fault segment and that the next earthquake will rupture the entire North Anatolia Fault system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Marmara sedimentary record is a powerful tool to constrain the earthquake history of the North Anatolia Fault, but the sedimentary record is still incomplete and more cores need to be collected in order to better constrain the earthquake record.
the sedimentary cores retrieved from the Sea of Maramara provide a record of the earthquakes that occurred along the Tekirdagh fault segment.
we obtained a paleoearthquake record for the western part of Sea of Marmar, which is the most hazardous part of the North Atlantic Fault.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tekirdag segment ruptured in the past, and that it is likely to rupture again in the future, with a recurrence interval similar to the one of the 1912 earthquake (300 yrs).
the sedimentary record can provide a reliable and cost-effective tool for paleoseismological investigations in the Sea of Maramara.
sedimentary cores are a powerful tool in paleoseismology, which should be used more extensively.
